messageCenterItems.title: Pay-as-you-go consumption-based meter for your extra SharePoint storage needs
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft is introducing a pay-as-you-go billing model for SharePoint storage overages, allowing admins to pay only for extra storage used beyond the included quota. This opt-in feature, rolling out globally in January 2027, integrates with Microsoft 365 Archive and requires Azure billing permissions.
messageCenterItems.body:
Updated November 9, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

Introduction

To help organizations manage SharePoint storage more flexibly and avoid over-provisioning, Microsoft is introducing a pay-as-you-go, consumption-based billing model for SharePoint storage overages. This option allows you to pay only for the additional storage you actually use, rather than pre-purchasing extra capacity. The experience integrates with Microsoft 365 Archive and helps align storage costs with real usage.

This change is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 506743.

When this will happen:

  • Public Preview (Worldwide): We completed rollout in June 2026.
  • General Availability (WW): We expect to begin rolling out in early January 2027 (previously early November) and to complete rolling by late January 2027 (previously end of November). 

How this affects your organization:

Who is affected:

  • Microsoft 365 administrators managing SharePoint Online storage
  • Note: This feature isn’t currently available to education tenants. Let us know if you’d like it to be supported in the future.

What will happen:

  • Admins can enable pay-as-you-go SharePoint storage billing in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
  • Storage used above the included tenant quota will be automatically billed based on consumption.
  • There is no impact to users.
  • The existing Office 365 Extra File Storage add‑on remains available if you prefer to manually increase your storage quota instead.
  • The feature is opt-in and off by default.

What you can do to prepare:

  • No immediate action is required. However, we recommend the following:
  • Review your tenant’s current SharePoint storage usage in the SharePoint admin center > Active sites.
  • Evaluate whether a consumption‑based model or manually purchased storage best fits your organization’s cost and governance preferences.
  • If you plan to enable pay‑as‑you‑go billing:
    • Ensure the appropriate Azure subscription and billing permissions are in place.
    • Update internal documentation or cost‑management processes as needed.
  • Share this information with finance or procurement teams if they track usage‑based charges.

Learn more: Add more SharePoint storage to your subscription | Microsoft Learn

Compliance considerations

Compliance areaImpact and explanation
Admin monitoring and reportingSharePoint storage usage above the included tenant quota will be reflected in consumption-based billing and usage reports, which may affect how admins monitor and track storage consumption and costs.
Admin controlAdministrators must explicitly enable

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Teams: Video sharing from OneDrive in Teams events
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Teams will soon allow event organizers and producers to share videos directly from OneDrive during Teams events using "Manage what attendees see," enabling smoother, higher-quality playback without screen sharing or embedding in PowerPoint. Rollout begins mid-November 2026, with no action required.
messageCenterItems.body:
Updated November 10, 2026: We have updated the timeline. If you are a tenant in a GCCH or DoD environment, you can safely ignore this message as you are not impacted. Thank you for your patience. 

What and why

Microsoft Teams will soon support sharing video directly from OneDrive during Teams events. Organizers and producers using Manage what attendees see can load videos from OneDrive and present them on stage without screen sharing a local media player or embedding videos in PowerPoint. This improvement provides smoother, higher-quality video playback for attendees and simplifies event production through built-in video playback controls.

Rollout schedule

  • Targeted Release (Worldwide): Rollout will begin in mid-November 2026 (previously early November) and end in early December 2026.
  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC): Rollout will begin in early December 2026 and is expected to complete by early December 2026.

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Teams event organizers and producers using events configured with Manage what attendees see.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams
  • OneDrive
  • Teams events

What will happen

  • Organizers and producers will be able to select and share videos stored in OneDrive directly within Teams events configured with Manage what attendees see and will have access to built-in controls to start and pause video playback during events.
  • Videos can be presented on stage without screen sharing a local media player or embedding videos into a PowerPoint presentation.
  • Attendees will experience smoother and higher-quality video playback.

Action required and recommendations

No action is required. We recommend that you:

  • Inform Teams event organizers and producers that they can share videos directly from OneDrive in Teams events configured with Manage what attendees see.
  • Ensure that organizers and producers store videos in OneDrive with the appropriate permissions before using them in events.
  • Review and update internal event production guidance that recommends screen sharing locally played videos or embedding videos in PowerPoint.

Learn more

We will update this post with new documentation.

Compliance considerations

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.
